themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Safety Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints surged to 6 THIS WEEK, a 220% jump from the 1.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.88), signaling a potential emerging public health concern in East Flatbush's food service sector that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 6 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (220% increase)
Z-score of 6.88 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Cluster timing suggests potential systemic issue rather than isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which establishments are under investigation and what violations triggered complaints
Interview residents about specific food safety concerns they've reported; map complaint locations to identify geographic hotspot

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped 243% to 9 complaints LAST WEEK, compared to a 2.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.44), concurrent with a 1500% spike in commercial disposal complaints 2 weeks ago, suggesting a district-wide sanitation infrastructure breakdown.
evidence: 9 residential disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.6 weekly average (243% increase, z-score: 7.44)
4 commercial disposal complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.2 weekly average (1500% increase, z-score: 5.67)
Sustained spike across both residential and commercial sectors suggests systemic failure, not isolated complaints
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation Department to determine if collection schedules have been disrupted or if equipment failures are affecting the district
Interview residents and business owners about garbage accumulation; photograph streets showing uncollected waste

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Tree Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints exploded this week and last week: 6 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK (2300% above 0.2 weekly baseline, z-score: 13.28) plus 14 damaged tree complaints (762% increase, z-score: 12.47), suggesting widespread environmental stress or disease affecting East Flatbush's urban canopy.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (2300% increase, z-score: 13.28)
14 damaged tree complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (762% increase, z-score: 12.47)
Combined 20 tree-related complaints in one week suggests single causal event (disease, pest, weather, contamination)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks Department to identify disease vectors or pest infestations affecting East Flatbush trees; request inspection data
Interview urban foresters about whether drought, salt application, or construction activity could explain mass tree decline; document species affected

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect Accelerates
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints spiked to 15 LAST WEEK, an 823% jump from the 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.47), indicating a potential breakdown in NYC Sanitation's street maintenance operations in East Flatbush.
evidence: 15 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly baseline (823% increase, z-score: 5.47)
Spike coincides with residential and commercial disposal complaint surges, suggesting coordinated sanitation service disruption
Sustained spike above baseline indicates ongoing rather than one-time operational failure
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation District 17 supervisor to determine if staffing shortages, equipment failures, or scheduling changes caused service interruption
Photograph uncleaned streets to document accumulation; interview residents about how long streets have remained unswepped

themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints surged to 4 LAST WEEK, a 3100% spike from a 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 11.72), suggesting acute electrical system failures or new infrastructure stress in East Flatbush.
evidence: 4 electrical complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (3100% increase, z-score: 11.72)
Extreme z-score indicates statistically rare event cluster
311 data does not specify nature of electrical failures (outages, exposed wires, overloaded circuits, etc.)
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison and NYC Department of Environmental Protection to identify reported electrical incidents; determine if outages or hazardous conditions occurred
Review FDNY incident reports for electrical fires or hazardous condition calls in East Flatbush aligned with complaint dates
